relationship.statement: For small swings, a pendulum's period depends only on its length and gravity, not on its mass or starting angle. Longer pendulums swing more slowly, while heavier bobs and wider small-angle swings take the same time per cycle.
assumptions: Gravity is fixed at 9.81 m/s^2 on Earth.
The swing angle stays small (20 deg or less) so sin(theta) approx theta.
Air resistance and pivot friction are ignored, and the rod is massless.

quantities.label: Length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot to the centre of the bob.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravitational acceleration held constant at 9.81 m/s^2.

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time required for one complete back-and-forth swing.

quantities.label: Angle
quantities.meaning: Current angle of the pendulum from vertical.

quantities.label: Speed
quantities.meaning: Current linear speed of the pendulum bob.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var g = 9.81; var L = inputs.length; var m = inputs.mass; var ampDeg = inputs.amplitude; var ampRad = ampDeg * Math.PI / 180; var omega = Math.sqrt(g / L); var period = 2 * Math.PI / omega; var theta = ampRad * Math.cos(omega * t); var thetaDot = -ampRad * omega * Math.sin(omega * t); var angle = theta * 180 / Math.PI; var bobX = L * Math.sin(theta); var bobY = -L * Math.cos(theta); var vx = L * thetaDot * Math.cos(theta); var vy = L * thetaDot * Math.sin(theta); var speed = Math.abs(L * thetaDot); var velTipX = bobX + 0.4 * vx; var velTipY = bobY + 0.4 * vy; var eqY = -L; var bobSize = 0.25 + ((m - 0.5) / 2.5) * 0.7; var isLong = L > 1.5; var isShort = L < 0.9; return { period: period, angle: angle, speed: speed, bobX: bobX, bobY: bobY, velTipX: velTipX, velTipY: velTipY, eqY: eqY, bobSize: bobSize, isLong: isLong, isShort: isShort }; }

outputs.meaning: Time for one full back-and-forth swing.
Current angle from vertical in degrees.
Current linear speed of the bob.
Horizontal coordinate of velocity arrow tip.
Vertical coordinate of velocity arrow tip.
Vertical position of the equilibrium point.
Visual size of the bob proportional to mass.
True when the pendulum length is over 1.5 m.
True when the pendulum length is under 0.9 m.

always: Only length sets the swing period.

cases.text: Long rod: slow swing, large period.
Short rod: fast swing, small period.

explanation.otherwise: Medium rod: ~2 s per full swing.

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum's swing?
lesson.description: Watch a simple pendulum swing while its angle is plotted over time. Adjust its length, mass, and release angle to see which ones change the period.
lesson.instructions: Use the sliders to change length, bob mass, and start angle. Watch the swing, the velocity arrow, the live period readout, and the angle-time graph as you test each variable.
lesson.goal: Discover that only length changes a small-angle pendulum's period, while mass and starting angle leave the timing unchanged.
